directives.name: Async Processing & Post-Click Wait Handling
directives.content:
When clicking a button or control that starts an asynchronous or long-running process, do not immediately continue to the next interaction.

After the click, wait for the resulting process to complete before continuing.

Examples include actions such as:
- Run Processing
- Run Screening
- Calculate
- Submit
- Generate
- Upload
- Import
- Refresh
- Validate
- Search
- Process
- Save and Continue
- Any action that displays a loading, processing, pending, spinner, progress, or disabled state.

Prefer condition-based synchronization rather than arbitrary fixed waits.

After clicking such an action:

1. Identify an observable indication that processing has started, where available.
2. Wait until processing has completed.
3. Wait for the expected resulting element, status, message, screen, or enabled control before continuing.
4. Add an assertion for the expected completion state when appropriate.

Example:

Click on "Run Processing"
Wait for "Processing completed"
Assert "Processing completed" exists

Or, if a processing indicator is shown:

Click on "Run Processing"
Wait for "Processing..."
Wait for "Processing completed"
Assert "Processing completed" exists

Do not continue interacting with dependent fields, buttons, or pages while processing is still in progress.

Avoid adding fixed waits such as "Wait 10 seconds" unless there is no reliable UI state or element that can be used to determine completion.

directives.name: Structured Raw Comment Handling
directives.content:
When a generated journey contains a large raw comment with multiple business actions, stages, fields, selections, or expected outcomes, do not treat the entire comment as one undifferentiated instruction.

Interpret the comment as multiple logical actions and expand it into structured executable Virtuoso NLP steps during Autopilot execution.

Use the business flow, screen/stage boundaries, and field groupings to separate the actions logically.

For example:
- Prospect Details
- KYC & AML
- Risk & Suitability
- Investment Preferences
- Service & Funding

Generate individual executable steps such as Write, Pick, Click, Wait, Look for, and Assert as appropriate.

Keep one UI interaction per executable step.

Use comments only as short section headers or business-intent descriptions when generating the final journey structure.

Do not leave required fields, variables, selections, validations, or expected outcomes only inside a long raw comment.

directives.name: KYC & AML – Dependent Dropdown & Screening Handling
directives.content:
For the KYC & AML form, dropdowns may trigger dependent field refreshes.
After selecting Identity document type, Source of wealth, or Source of funds:
- Wait for the form to stabilise.
- Verify the selected value remains selected.
- If another previously completed dropdown resets to "Select...", re-select it after the latest dropdown update completes.
Do not proceed to Run screening until all mandatory dropdowns contain the expected selected values.
After Run screening completes, verify mandatory dropdown values again before clicking Continue.

directives.name: Dropdown Selection Stability & Re-render Handling
directives.content:
When interacting with sequential dropdowns, validate that each selected value remains selected before moving to the next dropdown.
If selecting a dropdown causes the page or form section to re-render, wait for the UI to stabilise before continuing.
After each dropdown selection:
1. Wait briefly for any dependent UI update.
2. Assert that the selected option is still selected.
3. If a previously selected dropdown has reset to its default value, re-select it only after the triggering dropdown has finished updating.
Do not immediately interact with the next dropdown while the previous selection is still causing a page or component refresh.

directives.name: Recover from validation errors
directives.content: After activating Continue, if the step counter has not advanced, read the validation messages shown on the page, set the fields they name, and activate Continue again. Do not repeat the same Continue without changing a field.

directives.name: Element identification
directives.content: Identify elements by their data-testid attribute in preference to label text, placeholder or position. The test id index is in the source.
